notes:
**Windows** — run `ruze_0.0.17_x64-setup.exe`.
**Linux** — `flatpak install ruze-0.0.17.flatpak`, then `flatpak run com.ruze.chat`.
**Android** — sideload `ruze-0.0.17.apk`. arm64 devices, Android 8.0 or newer.

---

### Added

- **Friends, and a network that builds itself out.** Ruze knew about servers
  and about the people in them, and about nothing else: somebody you met in
  one was a name in a member list, and a server only ever reached you as an
  invite somebody thought to send. There is a friends list now, and it is the
  other half of that.

  Adding somebody is the pairing handshake's twin. You paste or scan the code
  from their account screen, their device puts a prompt in front of them
  naming the account asking — proved by the same certificate that membership
  rests on, not merely claimed — and on Accept the two devices exchange what
  they need to read each other.

  What they exchange is a *card*: one small document per account, holding your
  name, your avatar, whether you are here, and the servers you have chosen to
  publish. Each published server carries a real invite, so a friend joins it
  in one click — which is the point. Every server is published by default,
  with a switch of its own in its settings, and **a gated server is never
  published whatever the switch says**: publishing hands over a ticket, and a
  ticket to a gated server is read access to everything said in it.

  Your card also carries who you are friends with, and — only for the people
  whose own card says they allow it — the capability to read theirs. That is
  the whole of friends-of-friends: *Servers to find* lists what the people you
  know are in, and what the people they know are in, each credited to whoever
  it came through. The permission to be passed on belongs to the person being
  passed on; there is a switch for it beside the list.

  You can also ask somebody you are already in a server with: their profile
  card has the button, and the devices it dials are the ones their account
  certified in that server rather than whichever node id was on screen. The
  member list marks the people you already know, and their card offers a way
  straight into the conversation.

  And a conversation, per friend. Two one-way documents, one written by each
  side and merged by time — so neither of you can edit or delete a word the
  other said, because the capability to write those words was never yours.

  The namespaces for all of it are derived from the master key rather than
  created and remembered, which is what makes a card the same card on your
  phone and your desktop, and what lets a phrase typed into a fresh machine
  rebuild your side of everything. What cannot be derived is what other people
  gave you — their cards, their halves of your conversations — so those travel
  in the pairing handover too, alongside the servers.

  Worth knowing, and said on the button: a read capability cannot be taken
  back. Unfriending stops what you publish from reaching them and takes their
  card off this device. It does not unsay what has already been said.

- **Two shapes to choose between.** Ruze has always been one window with a
  rail of servers down its side, which is the right shape when servers are
  what you are here for and the wrong one when the people are — then the thing
  you actually watch is a list buried a click inside something else.

  Settings → Layout now offers the other shape: the friends list in a tall
  narrow window of its own, meant to be left open beside whatever you are
  doing. Your card sits at the top with the status menu on it, then a search
  box, then who is here and who is not — and the servers are docked at the
  foot of it. Clicking one brings the main window forward on that server, so
  the second window is a way back rather than a dead end.

  It comes back with the app, except on a launch straight to the tray, which
  is a launch meant to put nothing on screen — and the tray carries a
  **Friends** item in this shape, so a window you closed can be opened again
  without going through the one you were trying not to need. Your own picture
  at the top of it opens the profile panel.

  The choice is per device: the same account on a laptop and on a big monitor
  can want different answers. Desktop only — a phone has one window, and there
  is nowhere for a second one to go.

- **Your servers come with your account.** Linking a second device carried the
  account and nothing else — same name, same key, an empty sidebar, and every
  server left to be joined again from an invite you had to go and find. The
  device that approves a pairing now sends an invite for each server it is in,
  and the new device takes them up the moment the account lands. The panel says
  how many came across.

  The pins come too. A server's founding node and owning account are trust this
  device settled the first time it saw the server, and sending them means the
  new device inherits that rather than believing whichever peer answers it
  first. A server both devices were already in is left exactly as it is.

  One server that cannot be packed or taken up does not sink the pairing: it is
  logged and skipped, and can be joined from an ordinary invite later. And a
  device paired by an older Ruze, which sends the account alone, still pairs —
  it just arrives with the sidebar it always did.

  Worth knowing: approving a pairing now hands over write access to those
  servers as well as the account. Approving a stranger was already the worst
  thing that can happen here — the account is the greater thing by far — but it
  is one more reason to check that the six digits are the ones in your hand.

  A recovery phrase still cannot do this. There is nothing on the other end of
  a phrase to ask for the servers, which is why pairing is now the way across
  and the phrase is the fallback.

### Fixed

- **The Android update actually installs now.** Pressing *Download and
  install* threw immediately: the download never started, and what came back
  named a class that could not be found. That reading was true and the
  conclusion drawn from it was wrong. The class is in the APK; the trouble is
  where it was being looked for.

  A class named to JNI is resolved through the class loader of the Java frame
  beneath the call. A thread Rust attached has no Java frames — it was started
  by tokio, not by the runtime — so Android falls back to the *system* class
  loader, which knows the framework and nothing about this app. Every class of
  Ruze's asked for that way comes back missing, and the exception it raises is
  indistinguishable from one that a minifier really did strip. That is what
  sent 0.0.14 after R8 keep rules, which were not the problem and are not the
  fix.

  Classes are now asked of the activity's own class loader, which is the one
  that loaded the app. The voice call service was reached the same way and had
  the same fault, and it had it silently — a failure there is logged and
  swallowed, because a call still works on the screen in front of you and only
  stops when the phone is locked.

  While in there: the download names its destination through the API Android
  sanctions for it, the completed download's status is checked rather than
  inferred from a file existing, and unmounted storage is said out loud
  instead of dereferenced.

- **The friends window could not open a file dialog.** Choosing a profile
  picture there refused with a permission error naming the window. Capabilities
  in Tauri are granted per window, and a window added later gets none of them —
  so the second window had no file dialog, and no core plugin either, which is
  what its own event listeners run on. It has a capability of its own now: the
  core plugin and the dialog, and deliberately not notifications, which belong
  to the main window and would otherwise announce every message twice.

- **A profile picture is now checked before it is sent.** There was no limit
  and no check: any file, any size, under whatever name it happened to have.
  A picture is now read for what it actually is — PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP or
  AVIF, decided by the bytes rather than by the extension, which is a claim by
  whoever picked the file — and capped at 8 MB. Server icons are checked the
  same way, and both say so before you go looking for a file.

  It matters more here than for an attachment: an avatar reaches every member
  of every server you are in, is fetched to be drawn at forty pixels across,
  and is content-addressed — so there is no taking it back out of anybody
  else's copy.

- **Attaching a file on Android, and pasting an image anywhere.** The attach
  button on a phone opened the system picker, which answers with a
  `content://` URI — a row in another app's content provider, not a path — and
  the backend then tried to open it as a file and failed. Nothing about the
  error said which of those two things had gone wrong.

  The window now reads the file itself on a phone and passes the bytes over,
  four megabytes at a time, into a scratch file that becomes an ordinary
  attachment. Desktops keep the native dialog and its real path: it is faster,
  and nothing has to travel through the webview.

  The same road carries a pasted image, on every platform. An image on the
  clipboard was never a file on disk, so pasting one into the message box used
  to do nothing at all; it now goes as an attachment, while pasting text goes
  on being text.

### Changed

- **"Join an account" is now "Link an existing account".** Ruze already uses
  *join* for servers, so a button that said *Join an account* read like there
  was an account out there to be let into. What it actually does is put this
  device on the account you already have, which is what it now says — in
  account settings, in the pairing instructions that tell you what to choose on
  the other device, and on the welcome screen.
